sentences.text: 1. The present writ petition is a case of excessive executive actions on the part of the Respondent Authorities to deprive the Petitioner of her constitutional rights under Article 300A of the Constitution.

2. It appears from the records which has been duly admitted that the Petitioner herein who is 65 years old at present is the owner of a plot of land measuring 6 Bighas 2 kathas 17 Lechas covered by Dag No.288/292 of Patta No.195 of village Hahim under Luki Mouza of Boko Revenue Circle in the district of Kamrup (Rural).
It was alleged that in the year 1995, one Police Out Post namely Hahim Police Out Post under Boko Police Station was set up over 2 Bighas 1 Katha 13 Lechas of land of the Petitioner.

Thereupon, the Petitioner approached the Respondent Authorities on various occasions for release of the Page No.# 3/8 said land or to pay adequate compensation for utilizing her land for the Out Post.

The Respondent Authorities turned their deaf ear to the various requests so made and it was only after almost two decades, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Kamrup, Amingaon wrote a letter to the Superintendent of Police, Kamrup, Amingaon stating inter alia that the Petitioner's land was taken up for setting up the Hahim Police Out Post and the said Police Out Post has been possessing the land permanently but the Petitioner has not received any compensation.

sentences.text: request therefore was made that the Petitioner be paid the compensation for which an acquisition proposal be forwarded from the Office of the Superintendent of Police, Kamrup, Amingaon regarding the acquisition of the aforesaid land for Hahim Police Out Post.

Two months later, on 28.05.2013, the Superintendent of Police, Kamrup, Amingaon wrote a letter to the Additional Director General Police (A), Assam stating inter alia that in the land of the Petitioner, the Hahim Police Out Post has been functioning since 1995 however, there was no formal allotment of the said land and no compensation has also been paid to the owner.
It was therefore requested to accord approval to initiate the process for acquisition and taking official possession of the aforesaid land for Hahim Police Out Post.

The Deputy Inspector General of Police (Admn.) upon receiving the communication dated 28.05.2013 requested the Superintendent of Police, Kamrup, Amingaon vide a communication dated 05.07.2014 to submit a fresh proposal for taking action.

In the meantime,
the Petitioner continued to submit representation after representation but to no avail.
The record reveals that there were certain correspondences but nothing concrete happened.
It is under such circumstances, the Petitioner was compelled to approach this Court in the year 2017 by filing the instant writ petition.

3. The records reveals that pursuant to the issuance of notice, the Page No.# 4/8 Superintendent of Police, Kamrup (Rural) had filed an affidavit on 18.09.2017 admitting inter alia that the Hahim Police Out Post was established in the year 1995 and was situated over the land belonging to the Petitioner.
It was mentioned that various steps were taken for the purpose of making proposals for acquisition but nothing was done.
4. Various orders have been passed in the instant proceedings.

Relevant herein to mention that on 17.10.2023 when the matter was listed, it was brought to the attention of this Court that an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- was paid to the Petitioner as an interim compensation.

Under such circumstances,
this Court fixed the matter on 17.11.2023 directing the Respondents to apprise this Court as to whether any acquisition proceedings have been initiated in respect to the land of the Petitioner and if not, why.

5. The record reveals that on 17.11.2023, an instruction dated 10.11.2023 was placed before this Court which was kept on record and marked with the letter "X" to the effect that certain papers have been received from where it appears that the LA proceedings was initiated on 21.11.2019 and the matter was pending with the Home and Political Department for release of the balance amount.

Under such circumstances, when the said communication was placed, this Court directed the counsels representing the Respondent Authorities to apprise this Court on the next date as to whether the remaining compensation amount have been disbursed to the concerned authorities so that the same could be disbursed to the Petitioner.
Thereupon, the matter was listed on 08.12.2023 and 22.01.2024 however, no instruction was placed before this Court.
6. This Court further finds it relevant to take note of that on 02.02.2024, the instant writ petition was listed.

It was submitted by the Respondents that some Page No.# 5/8 acquisition process was initiated being L.A. Case No.12/2019 in connection with the acquisition of the said land for construction of the Hahim Police Out Post.
However, from the instructions, it was not clear as to whether any award was passed in that matter.

Under such circumstances, this Court fixed the Labaino Marak @ Labanya R. Marak @ ... vs The State Of Assam And 5 Ors on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9973125/
3 matter on 07.02.2024 with a direction to the Respondent Authorities to apprise as to whether any award has been passed in respect to the acquisition of the land of the Petitioner and if so, when it was passed.

sentences.text: This Court also directed to obtain instruction as to whether the possession had been taken in pursuance to such acquisition proceedings and when the possession was taken.

7. Today, when the matter is taken up, Mr. B. J. Talukdar, the learned Additional Senior Government Advocate had placed a set of instructions dated 12.02.2024 issued by the Additional District Commissioner, Kamrup, Amingaon.
From the instructions so received, it reveals that an acquisition proceedings was initiated being Land Acquisition Case No.12/2019.

It further reveals that from the said documents that the initiation of the acquisition proceedings have been shown on 10.11.2020 and on the basis thereof, an award was passed a 16.06.2021 thereby determining the Petitioner's entitlement of an amount of Rs.9,96,928.92p.
This Court had duly taken note of the awarded statement which reveals that the value of the land was taken as Rs.70,000/- per Bigha which corresponds to Rs.700/- per Lechas.

It is also seen that the determination of the compensation has been done under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "the Act of 2013") and the interest has been calculated in terms with Section 30(3) of the said Act of 2013 w.e.f. 10.11.2020 to 16.06.2021.
8.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: From the said materials on record, it also reveals that on 07.08.2020, much Page No.# 6/8 prior to the initiation of the acquisition proceedings, the land has been shown to have been taken possession.

However, strangely there is no mention whatsoever about the interest in terms with Section 80 of the Act of 2013 which stipulates interest @ 9% for the first year from the date of taking over possession and thereupon @ 15% after the completion of the first year.

This Court has made a specific query upon Mr. B. J. Talukdar, the learned Additional Senior Government appearing on behalf of the Respondents Authorities as to why the remaining amount of Rs.4,96,928.92p have not yet been paid in spite of the fact that the award was passed on 16.06.2021.
The learned Additional Senior Government Advocate however had no answer to the said query.

The said documents which has been placed before this Court is kept on record and marked with the letter "Y".
9.
From the above facts enumerated hereinabove, it would be seen that the Petitioner has been deprived of her constitutional rights to enjoy her property since 1995.

Admittedly, there has been no compensation paid as regards the unlawful and illegal possession of the Respondent Authorities over the land of the Petitioner since 1995 till the initiation of the acquisition proceedings on 10.11.2020.

Thereupon, it is further astonishing to note that although the award was passed as far back as on 16.06.2021 but no amount was paid to the Petitioner save and except an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- that too paid in the month of February, 2023 in view of the directions passed by this Court on 16.11.2020 as could be seen from a perusal of the order dated 28.02.2023 in the instant proceedings.

10. The above acts on the part of the Respondent Authorities clearly shows that the Petitioner's rights under Article 300A have been violated and if there was no direction passed by this Court on 16.11.2020 even the said amount of Page No.# 7/8 Rs.5,00,000/- would not have been paid.

It also appears that the Respondent Authorities have assumed that they have rights over the land of the Labaino Marak @ Labanya R. Marak @ ... vs The State Of Assam And 5 Ors on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9973125/
4

entities.text: Labaino Marak @ Labanya R. Marak @ ... vs The State Of Assam And 5 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner that too without proceeding in accordance with law.
This Court is also perplexed to observe that the Respondents herein included the Home Department of the Government of Assam.

The Home Department of the Government of Assam is In-Charge of the Police and if the Police Authorities resort to such high handed actions of depriving a citizen of her rights to the property, it shows a very sorry state of affairs.

11. Under such circumstances, this Court directs the Respondent Authorities more particularly the Respondent Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 4 to take immediate steps for payment of the remaining consideration of the amount of Rs.4,96,928.92p to the Petitioner forthwith and not later than 10 days from the date of the instant order.

12. Further to that, this Court directs the said Respondents to assess as to what amount the Petitioner would be entitled to as compensation for the period from the year 1995 till 09.11.2020 on account of the occupation of the Petitioner's land since 1995.
The said amount upon being assessed and determined be placed before this Court on the next date.

13. This Court further directs the said Respondent Nos. 1 to 4 to determine as to what amount of interest the Petitioner herein would be entitled to in terms with Section 80 of the Act of 2013 as on the next date and submit a report in that regard.

14. This Court further on the basis of the report so submitted on the next date shall take note of what consequential directions are required to be passed in respect to the erring officials which led to the violation of the Petitioner's Page No.# 8/8 constitutional rights under Article 300A of the Constitution and non-payment of the acquisition compensation amount in spite of the Award passed on 16.06.2021 which led to an unnecessary burden upon the State Exchequer.

15. List the matter again on 13.03.2024 as part-heard in the column of "top of the list".
